To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the amides of thiocarboxylate crown ethers are capable of undergoing methylation under the conditions of the reaction with methyl iodide and potassium hydroxide.

the amides of dibenzo-and benzo-crown thiocarbohydrazides are converted into the nitriles and dinitriles, respectively, of the corresponding benzo-crown and dibenzo-crown carboxy acids under the conditions that are typical for the synthesis of amides from carboxy acids.
the amides of thiocarboxylate crown ethers react with methyl iodide under the conditions of alkylation with formation of the corresponding carboxylic nitriles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of new compounds of benzo- and dibenzocrown acids, which are of interest for use in analytical chemistry.
the synthesis of new derivatives of dibenzo-, benzo-, and dibenzyldioxocrown ethers, and the investigation of the properties of the obtained compounds.
the development of a novel method for the preparation of nitriles and dinitriles, which are of interest in organic chemistry.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reaction of amides of thiocarboxylate acids with alkyl halides in the presence of bases is not always the expected reaction of alkylation.

the anomalous behavior of the benzo-and dibenzo-crown thiocarboamides is due to a nucleophilic attack of hydroxide ion on the sulfur atom of the thioamide group with subsequent elimination of the thiolate anion and the formation of the corresponding nitriles.
in the case of the amides, the reaction with the methyl iodide in alkaline media leads to the corresponding nitriles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nitriles are formed by an elimination reaction of the amide and the thiocarboxamide groups, which are in close proximity in the molecule.
the amides of thiocarboxylated crown ethers can be used to synthesize nitriles and dinitriles with crown ethers.
the amides of dibenzo crown thiocarboxlic acids are more stable than the benzo crown analogs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nitriles and dinitriles obtained from the reaction can be used for the synthesis of the corresponding crown carboxylic amides.
the reaction of benzo- and dibenzocrown amides with methyl iodide under the conditions of the methylation is not a simple methylation of the amide group, but it is a multistage process.
the reaction of the crown amides of thiocarboxylate acids with methyl iodine in the presence of KOH leads to the nitrile derivatives of the crown carboxylic acid.
